findings.title: Accidental git submodule of the repository itself committed
findings.body: The PR adds a new file `sentry-repo` containing `Subproject commit a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a` — this is a gitlink (embedded git repository) pointing at the base commit of this very repo, almost certainly created accidentally by running git commands inside a nested checkout. There is no corresponding `.gitmodules` entry, so this will leave the working tree in a confusing state for anyone who clones or checks out this branch (uninitialized submodule, dirty status, possible CI failures). It should be removed from the PR entirely.

findings.title: Substring match treats negated `!event.type:error` queries as error-focused and upsamples transaction counts
findings.body: _is_error_focused_query decides whether a discover query is error-only by checking `if "event.type:error" in query` on the lowercased raw query string. A query such as `!event.type:error` (everything *except* errors, i.e. transactions on the discover dataset) contains that substring, so it is classified as error-focused and count() is rewritten to `upsampled_count()` = `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))`. Transaction events do not carry a meaningful `sample_weight`, so their counts come back as 0/NULL instead of the true count — silently wrong results. The same false positive occurs for any query merely mentioning the text (e.g. `message:"event.type:error"`). The check should parse the query or at least account for negation rather than doing a raw substring match.

findings.title: Upsampling decision uses outer `dataset` instead of the `scoped_dataset` actually being queried
findings.body: Inside `_get_event_stats`, the eligibility check calls `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(snuba_params, organization, dataset, request)` where `dataset` is the closure variable from `get()`, not the `scoped_dataset` argument that the query is actually executed against. In the dashboard-widget split path (`get_event_stats_factory`), `_get_event_stats` is invoked with `discover` as the scoped dataset and an errors-only query (`({query}) AND !event.type:transaction`) while the outer `dataset` is `metrics_performance`/`metrics_enhanced_performance`; `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` then returns False for the metrics dataset, so error counts for allowlisted (client-sampled) projects are never upsampled and are under-reported by the sampling factor. The check should use `scoped_dataset` (and ideally the actual query string being executed rather than `request.GET`).

findings.title: Cache key built with `hash()` can collide across different project sets
findings.body: The eligibility cache key is `f"error_upsampling_eligible:{organization.id}:{hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids)))}"`. Python's `hash()` produces a 64-bit value with no uniqueness guarantee: two different sets of project IDs that hash to the same value share a cache entry, so one set's allowlist eligibility would be returned for a different set of projects, producing wrong (upsampled or non-upsampled) counts for up to 60 seconds. Hash values are also not guaranteed stable across Python versions, causing silent key changes on deploys. The sorted project IDs themselves (e.g. joined with commas) should be used as the key instead of a hash.

findings.title: Docstring claims fresh allowlist reads while the caller caches results for 60 seconds
findings.body: The docstring for `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` states: "This function reads the allowlist configuration fresh each time, which means it can return different results between calls if the configuration changes during request processing. This is intentional to ensure we always have the latest configuration state." In reality the only caller, `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`, caches the result for 60 seconds, so allowlist changes are explicitly *not* picked up fresh and stale eligibility is served for up to a minute. The docstring describes behavior the code does not have and contradicts the caching design documented in the caller; it should be corrected. Relatedly, `invalidate_upsampling_cache` (line 67) claims it "should be called when the allowlist configuration changes" but nothing in the codebase calls it, so there is no actual invalidation path.
